query: For high-entropy alloys used in thermal-insulation applications, what testable hypothesis could be made about an unspecified predictive approach for accurately identifying materials with low phonon thermal conductivity? The hypothesis should explain why the approach would work, predict its improvement over current predictions, define its applicability limits, identify supporting evidence, and specify a decisive experimental benchmark and outcome that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: A hybrid predictive framework that integrates machine learning models enriched with CALPHAD-derived thermodynamic and compositional descriptors with first-principles DFT-based phonon transport calculations will accurately identify high-entropy alloy compositions exhibiting exceptionally low lattice thermal conductivity. This approach works because the ML component efficiently screens vast compositional spaces for promising candidates, while the DFT component accounts for local lattice distortions and bonding variations that critically enhance phonon scattering.
generation.material_initial_state: Single-phase, compositionally well-defined high-entropy alloys (e.g., equiatomic or near equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi and its derivatives) where the baseline thermal conductivity is established through conventional processing.
generation.intervention: Application of the hybrid predictive framework to screen and predict promising HEA compositions followed by synthesis and measurement of their thermal transport properties.
generation.conditions: Synthesis of the predicted optimal HEA compositions under controlled melting/casting or powder metallurgy conditions; thermal conductivity measurements conducted over a temperature range of 300–800 K using standard techniques (e.g., laser flash analysis, TDTR); and complementing experimental data with X-ray diffraction for phase purity verification.
generation.structural_mediator: Local lattice distortions and chemical disorder emerging from the high-entropy effect, as well as subtle variations in bonding environments as predicted by DFT force constant calculations.
generation.mechanism: The approach improves predictions by combining data-driven correlations (capturing global compositional effects and thermodynamic stability) with atomistic insights into phonon scattering mechanisms. The synergy between the two methodologies allows the model to attribute reductions in phonon mean free path to specific lattice distortions and disorder, thereby narrowing prediction error margins compared to traditional empirical rules.
generation.predicted_outcome: Predicted HEA compositions will exhibit measured lattice thermal conductivities that are 20–30% lower than those estimated by conventional empirical approaches. The framework’s validity is confirmed if the measured thermal conductivity values are within a 10–20% deviation of the hybrid model’s predictions.
generation.baseline: Thermal conductivity values established from conventionally processed HEAs using standard empirical or simple phase diagram approaches.
generation.boundary: The framework is expected to be applicable primarily to single-phase HEAs with controlled compositional ranges where phase separation or severe inhomogeneities do not occur. Its accuracy may diminish in multiphase systems or when extrinsic defect factors dominate.
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainties remain regarding the precise numerical thresholds for improvement and the sensitivity of the ML models to limited data, especially in regions of compositional space with sparse experimental measurements. Further iterative validation between predictions and experimental results is required.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize a series of HEA compositions predicted by the hybrid framework and measure their lattice thermal conductivities across a range of temperatures (300–800 K). Perform parallel DFT calculations on these compositions to predict local phonon scattering mechanisms and compare the experimental results with these predictions.
measurements: Thermal conductivity using laser flash analysis or TDTR
Phase purity and microstructure via X-ray diffraction and TEM
Phonon density of states using in situ neutron or Raman scattering
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the experimentally measured lattice thermal conductivities deviate by more than 20% from the hybrid model predictions (or if key signatures of enhanced phonon scattering in the phonon density of states are absent), then the hypothesis that the hybrid predictive approach significantly outperforms conventional models would be falsified.

Recently, PbSnTeSe has been experimentally investigated by Fan et al. [] and Raphel et al. [,], who report appreciably similar results for the thermoelectric performance of the material (see below). The modelling of HEAs transport properties constitute a challenge, and both the simulation methods and their derived predictions have to be confronted to experimental data to assess their validity. In this context, we present in this paper for the first time a complete approach that allows one to obtain all the transport coefficients, including the figure of merit, of a high-entropy alloy. The thermoelectric transport properties of the PbSnTeSe high-entropy alloy have been calculated by combining state-of-the-art methods based on the special quasi-random structures approach to generate the HEA structure, the first-principles density-functional theory (DFT), and the Boltzmann transport and Green–Kubo theories. First, from the DFT-computed material electronic states, the electronic transport properties (electronic conductivity, Seebeck coefficient and electronic thermal conductivity) were calculated using the linearized Boltzmann transport equation, and the power factor was obtained. Our computations were performed within the DFT framework utilizing the projector augmented wave (PAW) [] technique, as implemented in the Vienna Ab Initio Simulation Package (VASP) [,,]. The Perdew–Burke–Ernzerhof (PBE) functional under the generalized gradient approximation (GGA) [] was utilized as the exchange-correlation functional. The nonempirical PBE functional is known to yield accurate crystal parameters and properties, and is known to fulfil many sum rules on the exchange-correlation hole []. Generally, where GGA functionals fail, local density functionals fail too. Concerning the thermal conductivity, compared to local density functionals, PBE does not over bind structures (it slightly under binds), hence the interatomic force constants are not too soft. cited_evidence.kind: web:3.5. Lattice Thermal Conductivity of PbSnTeSe
cited_evidence.text: Using the same approach, the value of κL was computed for various temperatures in the range 300–700 K (Figure 9). At 300 K, the κL value is 0.4 W K−1 m−1, which is a very low value of the lattice thermal conductivity, favorable for thermoelectric materials. This is due to the lattice distortion effect of high-entropy alloys that can reduce phonon velocity and enhance phonon scattering, resulting in low thermal conductivity. Additionally, one can observe that when the temperature rises, the thermal conductivity of the lattice decreases, which is also due to an increase in phonon scattering at higher temperatures.

proposals.intervention: Develop a first‐principles based computational framework that integrates density functional theory (DFT) with phonon Boltzmann transport calculations to directly predict phonon scattering rates based on local lattice distortions.
proposals.conditions: Perform DFT simulations at several temperatures (e.g., room temperature to 600°C) for fully relaxed, single‐phase microstructures; benchmark with laser flash thermal conductivity measurements.
proposals.structural_mediator: Atomistic lattice distortions and local bonding variations
proposals.mechanism: The hypothesis is that, in HEAs, the severe local lattice distortions statistically broaden the phonon density of states, leading to an enhanced phonon scattering rate. The predictive approach exploits DFT‐calculated force constants and local bond-distribution metrics to forecast low phonon mean free paths.
proposals.predicted_outcome: A predicted reduction in intrinsic phonon thermal conductivity by at least 25–30% over models that neglect lattice distortion, with measurements confirming thermal conductivities within a 10% margin of the computed values.
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: This direction explains why the predictive approach works (by capturing the lattice disorder at the atomic scale), provides quantitative improvement over traditional models that assume average properties, and sets clear temperature conditions and a measurable benchmark (thermal conductivity) that can falsify the hypothesis if the experimental values diverge significantly.

proposals.material_system: Modified CoCrFeMnNi-based HEA with isovalent doping (e.g., partial Al or Ti substitution)
proposals.intervention: Systematically vary the doping level (e.g., 0–10 at.%) to intentionally modify atomic size mismatches, and so tune the lattice distortion in the alloy using controlled solid-solution synthesis and subsequent homogenization heat treatments.
proposals.conditions: Prepare samples with precise doping levels via arc melting followed by homogenization at ~1100°C for 24 hours; assess using transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and X-ray diffraction (XRD) at room temperature; measure thermal conductivity with time-domain thermoreflectance (TDTR) over a range from 300 to 600 K.
proposals.structural_mediator: Controlled lattice distortion induced by doping
proposals.mechanism: The hypothesis posits that isovalent substitution increases local lattice strain and chemical disorder, leading to additional phonon scattering centers. The predictive approach would correlate the extent of doping-induced distortions with reduced phonon mean free paths, thus improving the identification of low thermal conductivity materials.
proposals.predicted_outcome: A consistent, measurable decrease in thermal conductivity (e.g., a 30% drop at optimal doping) relative to the baseline undoped HEA. A decisive benchmark is that if no systematic decrease is observed with doping levels, the hypothesis and accompanying predictive correlations would be falsified.
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: This approach not only tests the hypothesis that lattice distortion is a key parameter (explaining why the predictive approach works) but also defines its limits (optimal doping level) and provides a clear experimental benchmark (TDTR measured conductivity) for falsification.

proposals.material_system: Database of multicomponent HEAs spanning a wide compositional space (e.g., Co, Cr, Fe, Mn, Ni, with minor additions)
proposals.intervention: Integrate machine learning (ML) algorithms with CALPHAD-inspired parameters—including atomic size mismatch, valence electron concentration, and known phase boundaries— to predict compositions with intrinsically low phonon thermal conductivity.
proposals.conditions: Curate an extensive HEA dataset with known phase stability and limited thermal conductivity data; train ML models (e.g., gradient boosting regressors) on available data; then synthesize and characterize predicted optimal alloys under controlled melting and casting conditions and measure thermal properties from 300 to 800 K.
proposals.structural_mediator: Overall chemical disorder and phase homogeneity encoded in compositional descriptors
proposals.mechanism: The hypothesis is that machine learning models, when supplemented with thermodynamic parameters (as derived from CALPHAD) and electronic descriptors, can more accurately capture the effects of chemical complexity on phonon scattering. This combined approach should outperform empirical rules by quantitatively correlating compositional variables with thermal conductivity.
proposals.predicted_outcome: The ML model is expected to identify HEA compositions whose measured thermal conductivities are at least 20% lower than those predicted by traditional empirical models. Falsification would occur if the experimentally measured values deviate by more than 20% from the predictions.
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: This direction provides an explicit, testable hypothesis that integrates multi-parametric ML predictions with traditional thermodynamic data, clearly stating its improvement, limitations, and a definitive experimental benchmark for falsification.

proposals.material_system: Nano-engineered CoCrFeMnNi HEA with tailored grain boundary architectures
proposals.intervention: Employ severe plastic deformation (SPD) such as high-pressure torsion (HPT) followed by low-temperature annealing to create a controlled distribution of ultra-fine grains and nanocrystalline grain boundaries, which act as effective phonon scattering centers.
proposals.conditions: Subject samples to HPT at room temperature under 6 GPa for 10 turns, followed by annealing at ~400°C for 1 hour to stabilize the nanograin structure without significant grain growth; perform in situ neutron scattering and TEM at various temperatures (300–700 K) to observe phonon dispersion and microstructure evolution; measure thermal conductivity across the same temperature range.
proposals.structural_mediator: Enhanced grain boundary density and nanocrystallinity
proposals.mechanism: The hypothesis asserts that the increased density of grain boundaries from SPD will introduce additional interfaces that scatter phonons, lowering thermal conductivity. The predictive approach would account for the contribution of grain boundary scattering in a manner that extends current models which mostly consider atomic-scale disorder.
proposals.predicted_outcome: An experimental decrease in thermal conductivity by an additional 15–25% relative to conventionally processed HEAs. A decisive test is that, if neutron scattering shows no shift in the phonon density of states corresponding to enhanced boundary scattering, then the predictive hypothesis fails.
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: This approach offers a clear mechanism (grain boundary phonon scattering), an improvement metric over standard microstructures, defined processing conditions, and experimental benchmarks (neutron scattering phonon measurements) that can decisively falsify the hypothesis if unmet.

decision.rationale: Merging the ML-based (Direction B) and first-principles (Direction D) approaches yields a hybrid predictive framework that leverages both extensive compositional/thermodynamic descriptors and atomistic simulations to capture local lattice distortions. This integrated method explains why the predictive approach would work—it considers both the data-driven correlations (e.g., via CALPHAD-inspired descriptors and ML algorithms) and the physics of phonon scattering (via DFT-calculated force constants). The merged approach predicts that the framework will outperform current empirical models by identifying HEA compositions with thermal conductivities at least 20–30% lower than conventional predictions, is applicable primarily to single-phase, compositionally controlled HEAs, and offers clear experimental benchmarks (e.g., direct thermal conductivity measurements versus model predictions within a 10–20% tolerance) that can decisively falsify the hypothesis if not met.
